$comment: Authoritative rules constants for the Animal Friends TCG prototype. Read by src/engine. Section numbers refer to docs/ANIMAL_FRIENDS_TCG_DESIGN_REFERENCE.md.
name: Animal Friends TCG

deckbuilding.$comment: Prototype decision: the Deck Workshop lets a player build any 30-card deck from the Character and Event catalogue. Copy and Character limits keep a custom deck playable — a deck of pure Events could never pay its own requirements. Copies are further capped by the card's rarity (maxCopiesByRarity), which src/engine/power.js derives from its power-to-opportunity-cost rating: the cards that carry a game are the ones you may least often repeat.

victory.$comment: Every Statue grants a boon and imposes a burden that lasts as long as its Mayor controls it. Collecting Statues therefore taxes the town that is winning, which keeps a Statue lead from compounding into a runaway.

orientation.$comment: Section 5: non-upright Characters rotate clockwise one quarter turn at the start of their owner's turn: 180 -> 270 -> 0.

shifts.$comment: A working Character stays Busy for its full delay: it does not advance orientation at Ready while a shift is in progress. The shift produces Supply at the End phase in which its remaining delay reaches 0; the Character readies normally afterwards. An effect that readies a working Character completes its shift immediately.

market.$comment: Section 8. Whenever a card leaves the Capital City, deal from the Market Deck until the display is back to setup.capitalCitySize (top-up refill; the earlier refill-only-when-empty rule let the display silt up with unwanted cards). Reshuffle the City Dump into the Market Deck when the Market Deck runs out mid-deal; cards in use and Out of Play never return. Prototype addition: if no Capital City card has been gained for market.staleTurns consecutive turns (and nothing is pending), the display is swept (Statues return to the Market Deck, other cards go to the City Dump) and redealt.

auction.$comment: Section 8. An announcement opens an auction rather than a one-shot challenge. On your own turn you may raise any auction you are not already winning by making another upright Character Busy and bidding above the standing bid; there is no limit on rounds, but the required step grows by 1 every incrementGrowsEveryNRounds bids so a war converges. Every Character pledged to an auction stays Busy until that auction ends -- it does not advance at Ready and effects cannot ready it -- so a long bidding war costs a Mayor their whole workforce, and 'cannot bid any more' usually means 'has nobody left to bid with'. Because the players alternate turns, being the high bidder at the start of your own turn means your rival had a turn and declined to answer, so the auction resolves then. A bid is a real commitment: escrow is topped up to the bid when it is made, the winner pays it all, and the loser forfeits half (rounded up) of everything they escrowed.
auction.$pledgeLevelEscalatesComment: A Mayor's Nth pledge to a single auction (announcing counts as the first) must be at least rank N: the 1st pledge may be any rank, the 2nd must be Journeyman or better, the 3rd must be a Master. With three printed ranks that caps any one Mayor at 3 pledges to a given auction, and it escalates by strength rather than by a flat count, so a cheap Apprentice minted fresh every turn cannot fund an endless war the way a raw pledge-count cap could still be gamed. Once every Mayor still contesting the auction has pledged at the top rank, nobody can ever field a Character strong enough to raise again, so instead of resolving to the standing bidder the auction voids: the card is shuffled back into the Market Deck, all escrow is refunded in full with no forfeit, and every pledged Character is released to ready normally. Reads the same way for more than two players and for any future rank added above Master.

disruptions.$comment: Disruption cards are shared shocks in the Market Deck. They are never bought: the moment one is dealt into the Capital City it resolves against both towns at once and goes to the City Dump, and another card is dealt in its place. Disruptions dealt during setup are set aside without resolving, since there is no game state yet to disrupt.

unemployment.stackKnockdown: top card to Town Dump, next card to Unemployment, rest to Town Dump
unemployment.$comment: Anti-lockout guardrail (Section 2 / 12): a Character that has not yet been upright during one of its owner's turns cannot be targeted by an opponent's Unemployment effect.

deckOut.$comment: Not specified in the design reference; prototype decision.

simulation.$comment: Safety cap for automated playtests; a game that reaches the cap is scored by Statue count, then Supply.

assumptions: The second player starts with one extra card and no extra Supply (setup.secondPlayerBonusSupply / secondPlayerBonusCards). The earlier +2 Supply offset was tuned for the one-shot challenge; once Supply became ammunition for a multi-round auction it handed the second seat a 57% win rate, and 480-game passes put the first player at 50.0% with cards alone.

A player may have several auctions running at once (one per Capital City card); each may be raised any number of times, but only on the raiser's own turn and only by a player who is not already the high bidder. Each bid pledges another upright Character, and pledged Characters stay Busy until that auction ends.

Committed bids are escrowed as they are made. The winner pays their bid in full; the loser forfeits half of everything they escrowed (rounded up) and is refunded the rest, so bidding beyond your means still costs something.
Every Statue carries a burden as well as a boon; burdens apply while the Statue sits in that player's Victory Row.
Disruption cards resolve on reveal against both towns and are never purchasable.
The Market Deck is chosen at setup from three decks (First Boroughs, Boom Town, Hard Times); all three contain every Statue.
Upgrading keeps the stack's current orientation and re-triggers the new card's recruit abilities.
Readying a Character that is mid-shift completes the shift at once.
Reactive abilities (Rowan, Ombudsperson; Rumor Control; Emergency Reserve) are implemented as shields set on your own turn that last until your next turn starts.
When the player deck is empty, the Town Dump is shuffled into it.
Top-up refill: the Capital City is dealt back up to five cards as soon as a purchase resolves, so the Market Deck keeps flowing instead of waiting for the whole display to be bought out.
Stale market: if nobody gains a Capital City card for six consecutive turns, the display is swept and redealt so the game cannot stall on unwanted cards.

Every card carries a rarity computed from its power-to-opportunity-cost rating (src/engine/power.js): Common, Uncommon, Rare, Super Rare or Legendary. Rarity is not raw power — a card is rated power^0.6 x efficiency^0.4, so an efficient cheap card can out-rate an expensive one. Rarity caps copies in a town deck (3/3/2/1/1).
